text:
SQLpipe has three processes that run at the same time.

The reader connects to Postgres. It streams rows in batches. Each batch has a fixed row count. The reader sends batches to a channel.

The converter reads from the channel. It changes each batch into a Parquet row group. It writes the row group to a buffer. When the buffer is full, the converter sends the buffer to the uploader.

The uploader writes each buffer to S3 as one part of a multipart object. If a part fails, the uploader tries again. It uses exponential backoff. After three tries, the uploader stops and returns an error.

The three processes run in a pipeline. Back pressure from a slow stage stops the faster stages. This keeps memory use low.
